_readme: Ground truth for eval/vision-bench.mjs: what a careful human reader sees on each plate,
and the energy/macros they would expect a food tracker to report for it.
Every nutrient is a [low, high] BAND, not a point. Portion estimation from a single
uncalibrated photo is genuinely uncertain — a benchmark demanding one exact number would
reward overfitting to these 19 photos instead of measuring whether the app is useful.
The bands are what a dietitian would accept as 'that's the right answer for this photo':
roughly ±30% around the considered estimate, wider where the serving itself is ambiguous
(a whole pizza on a board, a pan of rice — you cannot know how much of it is one portion).
dishes[].id must exist in app/public/data/nutrition-db.json. `optional: true` marks a dish
that is genuinely in the photo but which a reasonable person might not log (tea, a garnish,
a condiment smear) — it never counts against recall, and naming it is never spurious.
Estimates use FNDDS per-100g values, so a miss here means the pipeline is wrong, not that
the arithmetic disagrees with a different food database.
_aliasNote: Applied to BOTH the expected and the predicted id before comparing. Only for distinctions a person would not make on a photo — every chutney is 'a chutney' — never for foods whose calories differ materially (plain dosa vs masala dosa are separate dishes and must be told apart).

dosa-thali.note: Steel thali: one very large plain paper-roast dosa rolled into a tube, a bowl of white coconut chutney, a bowl of sambar.

masala-dosa.note: Triangular masala dosa with a green-pea and onion filling on paper, plus three small bowls: red chutney, sambar, white coconut chutney.

idli-vada-thali.note: Steel thali: three idli, four medu vada, a bowl of sambar, a bowl of coconut chutney.

sliders-watermelon.note: Three small chicken-patty sliders in sesame buns with lettuce and tomato, watermelon wedges behind.

fried-rice-bowl.note: A steel bowl filled with egg fried rice with peas, carrot and spring onion. One generous serving.

dal-bowl.note: A white bowl of dal makhani garnished with onion rings and coriander.

north-indian-thali.note: A full spread: two poori, chana masala, raita, vegetable pulao, two gulab jamun, ice cream, two cutlets, onion-tomato salad, a glass of orange juice. The hardest case in the set — many small dishes, several outside the vocabulary.

pizza-detroit.note: Detroit-style pepperoni pizza on a board: one square slice pulled forward, the rest of the tray behind it. A person would log one or two slices.

paratha-pan.note: A single ghee-brushed paratha in a steel pan, coriander flecks visible.

samosa-chutney.note: Three samosas on a wooden plate, one broken open; bowls of green coriander chutney and dark tamarind chutney; two clay cups of chai.

biryani-pan.note: Close-up of a pan of biryani/ghee rice topped with fried onion, cashews and curry leaf. One serving is a fraction of what is visible.

collage-pizza-salad-fries.note: A three-panel composite: prosciutto-rocket pizza, caesar salad, thick-cut chips. No real plate — tests whether the app finds three separate dishes without a plate scale.

caesar-plate.note: Caesar salad on a white plate: romaine, shaved parmesan, croutons, an anchovy fillet, creamy dressing.

pancakes-berries.note: A stack of three pancakes under blueberry compote and icing sugar, with whipped cream and a pot of maple syrup.

enchiladas-queso.note: A plate of enchiladas buried under crumbled queso fresco with diced potato around the edge.

naan-closeup.note: One butter naan filling the frame, coriander and nigella seeds on top. No plate visible.

momos-chutney.note: Seven steamed meat momos on a white plate, two cut open, with a glass dish of red tomato chutney.

tortilla-espanola.note: Half a thick Spanish potato omelette on a dark glass plate.

kungpao-rice.note: Chicken stir-fry with onion, pepper and cashews spooned over a bed of white rice on a white plate.
